item.title: About Us
item.description: Our Story NiaVico began with a question many adult children quietly ask: “Are they really okay?” Our parents value their independence, and we want to respect that. But distance makes reassurance harder. The usual solutions never felt quite right. Daily calls can feel like check-ins. Cameras feel invasive. Medical alert pendants are reactive and often unused. Each option solves one problem while creating another. We’re three longtime software engineers — and fathers — navigating the same generational shift many families face.

item.title: Frequently Asked Questions
item.description: FAQ Find answers to common questions about NiaVico below. Is this a medical device? No. NiaVico is a wellness monitoring system designed to help families stay aware of changes in an aging parent’s daily routine. It is not a medical device, does not provide diagnoses, and should not be used as a substitute for professional medical care. Does it detect falls? NiaVico is not designed as a fall detection system. It monitors patterns of movement and daily routines over time.

item.title: Privacy & Security
item.description: Wellness, not medical NiaVico is a wellness monitoring system, not a medical device. It is designed to help families stay aware of routine changes in an aging parent’s daily patterns. It does not diagnose conditions, provide medical advice, or replace professional healthcare. If you have concerns about a loved one’s health, always consult with a qualified healthcare provider. No cameras. No audio. Ever. This is not negotiable. NiaVico will never include cameras, microphones, or any form of audio or video recording.

item.title: Who It's For
item.description: Whether you’re helping a parent live independently, coordinating with siblings, or supporting residents or clients in a professional care setting, NiaVico provides quiet, pattern-based awareness — without cameras or intrusive monitoring. For Families Most families don’t want more surveillance. They want better reassurance. When someone you love lives alone, small questions can grow heavy: Did they wake up at their usual time? Did they move through their normal routine? Was today a normal day?
